query: For example, LC-ESI-(+)-MS/MS fragmentation of dasc#3 [2'-(asc-C5)-asc-C4, 1], detected in P. degawai and P. fukushimae (Figures 2 and 4A), afforded an ion signal of C17H28NaO8+ (m/z 383.1667, [M + Na]+, Δ 2.4 ppm) with a loss of the C4 side chain (Supplementary file 2a—Figure 1), which helped to assign the first and the second ascarosides as ascr#9 [asc-C5] and ascr#11 [asc-C4], respectively (see Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B for details on the nomenclature of DASC chemicals).
